Local knowledge

L-Shaped Dormers on Lambeth Terraces

Behind the front walls of Brixton, Herne Hill and the Clapham borders are thousands of late Victorian and Edwardian terraces with a narrower two-storey rear return. Lambeth calls an L-shaped dormer a rear roof extension that projects out over that rear return, and says the aim should be to integrate it with the main roof and keep it subordinate to the house.1

The council's guidance is detailed. The L-shaped part should hold only one storey and stay below the main ridge. The end gable of the rear return should be kept, with slate hanging that follows its line. Party walls should rise in stock brick with a traditional parapet and brick-on-edge coping, and chimneys on the party walls should be extended at least eight brick courses above the roof.1 If you are also considering a rear mansard, Lambeth asks for both to be designed together.

Planning in Lambeth

Planning an L-Shaped Dormer in Lambeth

  • Conservation areas and heritage assets: Lambeth does not consider L-shaped rear return extensions appropriate. A modest rear dormer is the usual alternative.1
  • Elsewhere: an L-shaped dormer may be permitted development within 40 cubic metres on a terrace, and the section joining the rear return is exempt from the 20 cm eaves set-back.2
  • Neighbours: Lambeth checks for overlooking and loss of daylight from new windows, so we position them carefully.

What's included

Your Lambeth L-Shaped Dormer, Start to Finish

Survey, a design to Lambeth's guidance, volume calculation, lawful development certificate or planning, party wall notices to both neighbours, the build and building control sign-off. Our main L-shaped dormer loft conversion page covers the process and London costs.

The rear return section is also the natural home for a loft bathroom, because the first-floor bathroom on most Lambeth terraces sits directly below it. Putting the en-suite there keeps the drainage run short and leaves the main dormer free for a generous bedroom.

FAQ

Lambeth L-Shaped Dormer FAQs

Does Lambeth allow L-shaped dormers?

Yes, on suitable houses outside conservation areas. Lambeth's Design Guide says L-shaped extensions over a rear return are not considered appropriate on heritage assets or in conservation areas, so check your address before planning one.

What are Lambeth's rules for L-shaped dormers?

The L-shaped part should hold no more than one storey, be no higher than the main roof ridge, keep the end gable of the rear return with slate hanging following its line, extend party walls upwards in stock brick with a traditional parapet, and raise party wall chimneys at least eight brick courses above the roof.

Can I add an L-shaped section to my existing dormer?

Often, yes. Lambeth's guide says that where there is already a roof extension, the L-shaped part should integrate with it and copy its materials and detailing.
